name: worktree-colors
description: Gives every git worktree its own OKLCH-based window border / title bar color without touching the repo's .vscode folder.

commands.title: Worktree Colors: Reset to Default Color
Worktree Colors: Remove Colors From This Window

worktreeColors.lightness.markdownDescription: OKLCH lightness (0–1) shared by all worktree colors. Text switches to black above `0.65`.

worktreeColors.chromaMin.markdownDescription: Lowest OKLCH chroma a worktree can get. Each worktree's chroma is picked from the hash between `chromaMin` and `chromaMax`.

worktreeColors.chromaMax.markdownDescription: Highest OKLCH chroma. At lightness `0.5`, up to about `0.085` fits in sRGB for every hue; above that, some hues are toned down to fit the screen.

enumDescriptions: Color follows the branch name: a re-created worktree for the same branch gets the same color. Falls back to the path when HEAD is detached.
Color follows the worktree's folder path.
worktreeColors.hashSource.description: What the color is derived from.

enumDescriptions: Window border and sash hover border.
Status bar (bottom), incl. hover, remote indicator and debugging state.
Activity bar (left, or top when moved there), incl. badges.

worktreeColors.targets.description: Which parts of the window get colored.

worktreeColors.colorMainWorktree.description: Also color the main worktree (the original checkout), not just linked worktrees.

enumDescriptions: Reopen each worktree through a generated .code-workspace file kept in the extension's own storage. The repo's .vscode folder is never touched.
Write the colors to the worktree's .vscode/settings.json (only if that file is not shared).
worktreeColors.storage.description: Where the per-worktree colors are stored.

worktreeColors.mirrorRepoSettings.description: Mirror the repo's shared .vscode/settings.json into the generated workspace file and keep it in sync, so window-level shared settings still apply.

worktreeColors.replaceRepoColors.markdownDescription: Remove every color key this extension manages (for example leftovers from Peacock) from the repo's mirrored `workbench.colorCustomizations`, even for targets that aren't enabled. Other repo color customizations are kept.

worktreeColors.autoReopen.description: When a worktree is opened as a plain folder, switch to its colored workspace automatically instead of asking.
